The battle for new development teams, leaders, and strategists to overcome a prior corporate culture of “keep everything, just bolt the new stuff on” is a challenge in, I believe, every sector.

My recommendation is always to view the prior investment as what was needed when the investment was made–the money was spent and the application (I assume) met business needs. However, take notice that a new (direction, requirement, management staff) now requires another investment if the prior application doesn’t meet the needs. The old mainframe application may have worked great at the time, but that doesn’t mean it shouldn’t be redesigned to meet today’s needs.
